bottlenecks.config: LoFi, BF16 x BFP4 => BFP8, 64 cores
bottlenecks.verdict: already minimal fidelity (LoFi) + minimal weight dtype (BFP4). No further dtype/fidelity headroom without accuracy loss.

bottlenecks.config: LoFi, BFP8 x BFP4 => BFP8, 64 cores
bottlenecks.verdict: already LoFi + BFP4 weights. Optimal for speed.

bottlenecks.config: HiFi2, BF16 x BFP8 => BF16, 64 cores
bottlenecks.verdict: intentionally HiFi2 + BFP8 (accuracy-sensitive Q/K/V). Dropping to LoFi/BFP4 risks decode PCC < 0.99. Keep.
already uses sharded fast path (HiFi4 + fp32_acc + packer_l1) per dots_ocr_decoder_layer. Optimal.

structural layout-shuffle overhead. Only reducible by reworking the sharding/head-split strategy -- HIGH RISK on a tuned faithful port. Not recommended without a dedicated re-tune + full PCC re-validation.

recommendations.rationale: The ported implementation is the tuned production config: gate_up/down at LoFi+BFP4 (max speed), QKV at HiFi2+BFP8 (accuracy preserved). Matmul fidelity/dtype is already at the speed/accuracy Pareto front. Lowering QKV fidelity is the only dtype lever and it threatens the validated decode PCC>=0.99.
Reducing Permute/Slice/reshard overhead requires sharding-strategy rework, high regression risk on a validated port. Track as a future structural-perf item, not a config-override change.

config_optimize_rationale: Per decision profile (functionality first, then speed) the ported decoder already passed PCC>=0.99 AND carries the reference's tuned per-op configs. Applying further config overrides has near-zero speed headroom on the matmuls and material risk of regressing the validated PCC. config_optimize is therefore a validated no-op: current config IS the optimal config.
